raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Overview Install `infiniband-diags` (provides `ibstat`) in the runtime image, verify it at build time, and document it as a prerequisite for multi-node DeepEPv2. Fixes #62677. ## Claims - The final `vllm-openai` image contains a working `ibstat`; the image build fails if it doesn't. - Multi-node `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` no longer fails with `ZeroDivisionError` in `get_theoretical_num_sms()` because `ibstat` is missing. - Docs explain that `ibstat` must be available inside the container and that DeepEP reads the NIC named by `EP_NIC_NAME` (default `mlx5_0`). ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files `: passed. - `infiniband-diags` is in Ubuntu universe for 24.04 (50.0) and 22.04 (39.0), on amd64 and arm64. `ffmpeg` is installed from universe in the same stage. - `ibstat --version` exits 0 before it opens any device (rdma-core `ibdiag_common.c`), so the build check works on builders without InfiniBand. Deployment: 2 nodes × 8 B300, GLM-5.3, TP=8, DP=2, EP=16, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`, Kubernetes LeaderWorkerSet. | Check | Command | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Image build | `docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --target vllm-openai .` | TODO | | `ibstat` in image | `docker run --rm --entrypoint ibstat --version` | TODO | | NIC visible (leader pod) | `ibstat "${EP_NIC_NAME:-mlx5_0}"` | TODO | | NIC visible (worker pod) | `ibstat "${EP_NIC_NAME:-mlx5_0}"` | TODO | | Startup | no `Failed to get RDMA connection speed`; server ready | TODO | | Inference | `curl .../v1/completions` with `max_tokens=16` | TODO | CI does not exercise multi-node DeepEPv2; only the image build covers this change. ## Details Root cause (DeepEP `d4f41e4e93`, pinned in `docker/Dockerfile`): `deep_ep/utils/envs.py::get_rdma_gbs()` runs `ibstat` and returns `0` on any failure. `ElasticBuffer.get_theoretical_num_sms()` then divides by it. vLLM calls this from `DeepEPV2All2AllManager.get_handle()`. `check_fast_rdma_atomic_support()` also runs `ibstat` and silently returns `False` without it, which changes QP allocation. Catching the exception in vLLM is not enough because the SM count depends on the detected bandwidth. Guarding the zero belongs upstream in DeepEP. --- --- Need help on this PR? detail.title: [Build] Install infiniband-diags for DeepEPv2 RDMA bandwidth detection

files.patch:
@@ -787,13 +787,16 @@ RUN apt-get update -y \
         python${PYTHON_VERSION}-dev \
         python${PYTHON_VERSION}-venv \
         libibverbs-dev \
+        # ibstat, used by DeepEPv2 for RDMA bandwidth detection
+        infiniband-diags \
     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
     && update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION} 1 \
     && update-alternatives --set python3 /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION} \
     && ln -sf /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION}-config /usr/bin/python3-config \
     && rm -f /usr/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/EXTERNALLY-MANAGED \
     && curl -sS ${GET_PIP_URL} | python${PYTHON_VERSION} \
-    && python3 --version && python3 -m pip --version
+    && python3 --version && python3 -m pip --version \
+    && ibstat --version
 
 # Install CUDA development tools for runtime JIT compilation
 # (FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, EP kernels all require compilation at runtime)

@@ -17,6 +17,11 @@ The edges of the build graph represent:
 
 - `RUN --mount=(.\*)from=...` dependencies (with a dotted line and an empty diamond arrow head)
 
+The `vllm-runtime-base` stage installs the system packages that the final
+images need at runtime, including `infiniband-diags`, which provides the
+`ibstat` executable that multi-node DeepEPv2 uses to detect RDMA bandwidth.
+The build runs `ibstat --version` to verify it.
+
 The `test-deps` stage branches from `vllm-runtime-base` so Git and the test
 requirements remain cached independently of per-commit vLLM wheels and source.

@@ -217,6 +217,7 @@ For multi-node deployment, add these EPLB flags to each node's command. We recom
 
 - **`non-zero status: 7 cannot register cq buf`**: When using Infiniband/RoCE, make sure host VM and pods show `ulimit -l` "unlimited".
 - **`init failed for transport: IBGDA`**: The InfiniBand GDA kernel modules are missing. Run `tools/ep_kernels/configure_system_drivers.sh` on each GPU node and reboot. Also fixes error `NVSHMEM API called before NVSHMEM initialization has completed`.
+- **`Failed to get RDMA connection speed` followed by `ZeroDivisionError` in `get_theoretical_num_sms`**: Multi-node `deepep_v2` could not read the NIC rate from `ibstat`. Install `infiniband-diags` inside the container (the vLLM images include it) and make sure `ibstat` lists the NIC named by `EP_NIC_NAME` (default `mlx5_0`). See the [EP kernels guide](../../tools/ep_kernels).
 - **NVSHMEM peer disconnect**: Usually a networking misconfiguration. If deploying via Kubernetes, verify that every pod runs with `hostNetwork: true`, `securityContext.privileged: true` to access Infiniband.
 
 ### Benchmarking

@@ -51,6 +51,22 @@ When NCCL is too old at runtime, vLLM logs the reason at startup and
 python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason; print(deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason() or 'deepep_v2 is available')"
 ```
 
+## `ibstat` requirement for multi-node DeepEPv2
+
+Multi-node `deepep_v2` runs `ibstat` (from the `infiniband-diags` package) to
+detect the RDMA bandwidth of the NIC named by `EP_NIC_NAME` (default `mlx5_0`).
+If `ibstat` is missing, or the NIC does not appear in its output, workers log
+`Failed to get RDMA connection speed` and fail with `ZeroDivisionError` in
+`get_theoretical_num_sms()`.
+
+The vLLM Docker images include `infiniband-diags`. For custom images, install
+it inside the container; installing it on the host is not enough:
+
+```bash
+apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends infiniband-diags
+ibstat "${EP_NIC_NAME:-mlx5_0}"  # should report the port Rate
+```
+
